Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_WDF_Europe_Cup_Youth) | Boys pairs | | **Luke Littler** (born 21 January 2007) is an English professional [darts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darts) player who competes in [Professional Darts Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_Darts_Corporation) (PDC) events, where he is ranked [world number one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_Order_of_Merit). Nicknamed " **the Nuke**", Littler has won two [PDC World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Championship), in [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PDC_World_Darts_Championship) and [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_PDC_World_Darts_Championship), and is the youngest world champion in darts history (17 years, 347 days). After winning the [2023 PDC World Youth Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_PDC_World_Youth_Championship) and five [PDC Development Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_Development_Tour) titles, Littler made his PDC World Championship debut in [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_PDC_World_Darts_Championship), aged 16; as a [66/1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odds) outsider, he reached the final and was defeated by [Luke Humphries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Humphries). He defeated [Michael van Gerwen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_van_Gerwen) to claim his maiden World Championship in [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PDC_World_Darts_Championship), when he [won six of 10 majors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_in_PDC)—including the [World Matchplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Matchplay)—and became the youngest world No. 1 at the [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Grand_Slam_of_Darts). He retained his world title in [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_PDC_World_Darts_Championship), defeating [Gian van Veen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gian_van_Veen) and becoming the eighth player to win successive [world titles in darts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Professional_Darts_Championship) and the fourth in the PDC, and has won [four further majors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_in_PDC), as well as the [PDC World Cup of Darts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_PDC_World_Cup_of_Darts). ## Career ### 2025: World champion and world number one Littler entered the second round of the [2025 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PDC_World_Darts_Championship) as the fourth seed,[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Littler#cite_note-72) where he defeated [Ryan Meikle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Meikle) 3–1 in sets. [[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Littler#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Littler#cite_note-74) Littler reached the final by defeating Meikle, [Ian White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_White_(darts_player)), [Ryan Joyce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryan_Joyce), [Nathan Aspinall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Aspinall) and [Stephen Bunting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Bunting). In March, Littler won the [UK Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UK_Open) for the first time, defeating [James Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Wade) 11–2 in the final. [[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Littler#cite_note-83) On Finals Night on 29 May, he defeated [Gerwyn Price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerwyn_Price) 10–7 in the semi-finals and progressed to the final where he played Luke Humphries in a rematch of the [2024 final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Premier_League_Darts). 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PDC_Players_Championship_series#Players_Championship_32), beating [Dennie Olde Kalter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennie_Olde_Kalter) 8–2 in the final. ## # PDC World Youth Championship
He and [Dimitri van den Bergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimitri_van_den_Bergh) (the 2017 and 2018 champion) are the only players to have won the World Youth Championship twice. Three of the thirteen World Youth Champions ( [Michael Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Smith_(darts_player)), [Luke Humphries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Humphries) and [Luke Littler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Littler)) have gone on to become senior World Champions, while three more ( [Josh Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Rock), van den Bergh and van Veen) have won other televised PDC titles.

## History
Van Gerwen once again finished runner-up in 2012, losing to [James Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Hubbard_(darts_player)).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-:4-12) [Michael Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Smith_(darts_player)) and Keegan Brown were the next two champions, with Smith later becoming the first Youth World Champion to become a senior PDC World Champion.

[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-14) Here, [Max Hopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Hopp) became the first German (and first player from outside England) to win the World Youth Championship, beating [Nathan Aspinall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Aspinall) 6–5 in a tight final which remained on throw until the final leg, where both players had match darts.

In 2019, [Luke Humphries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Humphries) became the second future senior World Champion to win the World Youth Championship, beating 17-year-old [Adam Gawlas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Gawlas), who qualified for the tournament despite having only played darts for nine months at the time. [[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-22) In 2020, the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic) meant that the Players Championship Finals (and thus the World Youth Championship final) were moved from their regular location in Minehead to the [Ricoh Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricoh_Arena) in [Coventry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coventry), where [Bradley Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_Brooks) won the title. [[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-24) In 2021, the size of the field was reduced and the tournament was played on a single day in Minehead.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-25) [Ted Evetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Evetts) became the only player to win in the one-day format, as the tournament returned to its previous schedule in 2022. [[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Youth_Championship#cite_note-26) Northern Irish player and future [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PDC_World_Cup_of_Darts) winner [Josh Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Rock) broke the streak of English winners in 2022, recording the highest three-dart average in a World Youth Championship final to date, 104.13.
